content.text: We have five security issues as issues candidates under https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/b8vNGrME7 . The fourth is already implemented in the branch Restrict_my_accounts. (not pushed by name but nonetheless public.) I would want to work on the other four, in order, on local branches even if they're not linear tasks yet.

{"guidelines":"# roam/agent guidelines <roam uid="XcDxM3AGm" refs="10"/>

- This is the **discourse-graphs team graph** (dg-team). It tracks product development, user research, and design knowledge for the Discourse Graphs project. Start orientation at [[🚪 Discourse graphs front page for team members]]. <roam uid="ZyEFQdPzy"/>
- Graph Ontology <roam uid="CkMv_I9Hu" heading="2"/>
  - This graph uses a discourse graph node grammar with typed nodes. Each node type has a title format that the Roam plugin uses for identification via regex. Nodes exist at two levels of formality: <roam uid="JZ-ERybz9"/>
    - **Full node pages** — titled with the type prefix (e.g., `[[ISS]] - description`). These are the primary knowledge units. <roam uid="Lr2QOC061"/>
    - **Candidate nodes** — blocks tagged with a candidate hashtag (e.g., `#iss-candidate`, `#res-candidate`). These are seedling ideas not yet promoted to full pages. <roam uid="IxTd36BlH"/>
  - Node Types: Knowledge <roam uid="iJARoph1H" heading="3"/>
    - **Question (QUE)** — the unknowns being explored through pilots and research. Format: `[[QUE]] - {content}`. Sections: Summary, Notes, Testable hypotheses, Snippets. <roam uid="9uXF_YcQQ"/>
    - **Hypothesis (HYP)** — proposed answers to questions; collect evidence for or against. Format: `[[HYP]] - {content}`. Candidate tag: `#hyp-candidate`. Sections: Rationale, Snippets, Requests for Experiments. <roam uid="jA0VLkwMY"/>
    - **Result (RES)** — a discrete observation from ongoing research, in past tense. Format: `[[RES]] - {content} - {Source}`. Candidate tag: `#res-candidate`. Sections: Summary, Grounding Context, Snippets. Properties: NodeFormality (Draft → ReadyForInternal → ReadyToShare → Published), Contributors. <roam uid="21s0GTu6p"/>
    - **Evidence (EVD)** — a discrete observation from a published dataset or experiment. Format: `[[EVD]] - {content} - {Source}`. Sections: Evidence Description, Snippets, Grounding Context, Centrality slider. <roam uid="zgYL5nVb4"/>
    - **Claim (CLM)** — an assertion about how discourse graphs work or should work. Format: `[[CLM]] - {content}`. Candidate tag: `#clm-candidate`. <roam uid="9SOQK_533"/>
    - **Source (SRC)** — a referenced publication or external resource. Format: `@{content}`. <roam uid="wenbahwqN"/>
    - **Theory (THE)** — a theoretical framework or model. Format: `[[THE]] - {content}`. <roam uid="UtoPH2BxJ"/>
  - Node Types: Product & UX <roam uid="e-gV24nNQ" heading="3"/>
    - **Function (FUN)** — a UX "use case": a specific situation where Discourse Graphs can be used to enhance the experience. Tool-agnostic in framing, but tied to a concrete user goal. Format: `[[FUN]] - {content}`. Properties: FunctionImportance, FunctionScoping. <roam uid="LjYlqRpUR"/>
    - **Flow (FLO)** — a set of interactions the user performs to accomplish a goal within a particular implementation of Discourse Graphs (Obsidian plugin, Roam plugin, tldraw, etc.). A Flow is the tool-specific instantiation of a Function/Use Case. Format: `[[FLO]] - {content}`. Sections: Description (Goal, Loom, brief description), Steps (Normal flow, Alt flows, Exceptions), Examples, Pain points. Properties: FlowStatus (💭 Hypothetical → 🗓️ Planned → 🤔 Experimental → 🚧 Bespoke → 🔨 Alpha → 🚀 Beta), FlowFrequency, FlowImpact. <roam uid="SVcbz9E3i"/>
    - **Artifact (ART)** — the features, workflows, and UI components we build to enable Flows and Use Cases (Functions). Parts of a system are prefixed with the system name (e.g., `[[ART]] - Roam DG/Query`). Format: `[[ART]] - {content}`. Properties: ArtifactType (Feature/Component or Workflow/Template), ArtStatus (🤔 Prospective → 🖇️ Bespoke → 🧪 Alpha → 🎯 Beta → 💎 Release → 🌐 External). <roam uid="71FJwPgwi"/>
    - **PainPoint (PAI)** — problems, friction, and bottlenecks in user experience. Format: `[[PAI]] - {content}`. Properties: Activity, Function, Flow, UserTool. <roam uid="zD3lBBh9A"/>
    - **Journey (JOU)** — a user journey across multiple functions/flows. Format: `[[JOU]] - {content}`. Sections: Description, Phases, Pain points, Notes. <roam uid="YmhUG6VJX"/>
    - **Activity (ACT)** — an action the user performs that is not specific to any particular tool or method (e.g., "synthesize literature," "discuss findings"). Activities sit upstream of tool-bound Flows and Use Cases. Format: `[[ACT]] - {content}`. <roam uid="1NcVa1g2X"/>
    - **UserPilot** — a specific user or pilot engagement. Format: `UserPilot/{content}`. Properties: User status, UserTool (Roam, Obsidian, Notion, tldraw), UserType (Alpha/Beta/Normie), Lead. <roam uid="5XUZyDshG"/>
    - **CaseStudy (CAS)** — a documented case study. Format: `[[CAS]] - {content}`. <roam uid="ceCyzY2Ei"/>
  - Node Types: Project Management <roam uid="L4Lo_4B1w" heading="3"/>
    - **Issue (ISS)** — a potential action item for development or research. Format: `[[ISS]] - {content}`. Candidate tag: `#iss-candidate`. Properties: Issue Status (🤔 Considering → 🗓️ Backlog → 🗓️ Planned → 🚀 Active → 💬 Awaiting Feedback → ➡ Sent To Linear → ✅ Complete → 🧊 Iced → ⏸️ On hold), Issue Type (🗳️ Feature Request, 📄 Template improvement, 🐞 Bug Report, 🔬 Research, 🏗️ DG team, 🛠️ Maintenance), Priority, Project, Function, Flow, Lead. <roam uid="jzczOjTM1"/>
    - **Project** — a research or development project. Format: `Project/{content}`. Properties: Project Status (🗓️ Backlog → 🗓️ Planned → 🚀 Active → ✅ Complete → 🧊 Iced → ⏸️ On hold), Priority. <roam uid="IwUFa4By7"/>
    - **Milestone** — a time-boxed delivery target. Format: `Milestone/{content}`. Properties: Milestone Status, Start/End Date, Priority. <roam uid="NCfJPwcoO"/>
  - Relation Types <roam uid="PZxB_Lim1" heading="3"/>
    - **Supports / Supported By** — Evidence or Result supports a Claim, Hypothesis, or Conclusion <roam uid="QLrw6Cikm"/>
    - **Opposes / Opposed By** — Evidence or Result contradicts a Claim, Hypothesis, or Conclusion <roam uid="RdGHvBjvu"/>
    - **Informs / Informed By** — Evidence, Result, or Claim informs a Question or Hypothesis; Question informs Hypothesis; Hypothesis informs Issue <roam uid="0TFxQSHzV"/>
    - **Reproduces / Reproduced By** — Evidence confirms other Evidence <roam uid="lZNpV65LF"/>
    - **Resolves / Is resolved by** — Result resolves an Issue <roam uid="BKCUPTVYB"/>
    - To query typed relations programmatically, use `mcp__discourse__get_relationships uid=…` (the `discourse` MCP) — it returns a node's Supports / Opposes / Informs / Reproduces / Resolves edges and their complements directly. See **Which MCP tool for which task** under Navigating. The `roam` MCP can't resolve typed relations; with it, fall back to following page references within node content and checking linked references. <roam uid="4uQA80UCZ"/>
- Navigating the Graph <roam uid="I5GtkN5Cn" heading="2"/>
  - Which MCP tool for which task <roam uid="0w3wW5Rny" heading="3"/>
    - Two MCP servers read this graph. Reach for the **`discourse`** server whenever a task depends on the discourse-node / relation grammar (typed nodes, typed relations, the ontology); use the **`roam`** server for general text search, reading arbitrary pages, and all writes. <roam uid="v7YWcac84"/>
    - **Find discourse nodes by topic** → `mcp__discourse__search_nodes` (all query words must appear in the node title; optional `node_type_format` regex restricts to one type, e.g. `\[\[FLO\]\]` for Flows). For free-text across __all__ blocks — meeting notes, daily notes, non-node content — use `mcp__roam__search` instead. <roam uid="OmYGreM1F"/>
    - **List every node of a type** (all Flows, all Issues, …) → `mcp__discourse__get_all_discourse_nodes` (optional `since` ISO date for "what's new"). More reliable than a roam prefix search, which can miss nodes. <roam uid="OMwgWxWHS"/>
    - **Read a node's full content** → `mcp__discourse__get_node uid=…` for the title + full block tree; `mcp__roam__get_page` / `mcp__roam__get_block` are the general-purpose equivalents. <roam uid="2LarSnz-g"/>
    - **Find a node's typed relations** (what Supports / Opposes / Informs / Reproduces / Resolves it) → `mcp__discourse__get_relationships uid=…`. Resolves the typed edges directly; the roam server cannot. <roam uid="GS3OMHszL"/>
    - **Walk a node's neighborhood** (multi-hop reference graph) → `mcp__discourse__get_node_neighborhood uid=… depth=1–4 direction=both`. <roam uid="ur9V-QLL7"/>
    - **Get the live ontology** (node types + relation definitions) → `mcp__discourse__get_discourse_node_types`. The source of truth behind the **Graph Ontology** section above — pull it when you suspect the documented types or relations have drifted. <roam uid="qVG4hiqaO"/>
    - **General text search, recency, reading arbitrary pages, and all writes** → the **`roam`** server: `mcp__roam__search` (empty query = recently edited / viewed), `get_page`, `get_block`, `get_backlinks`, `create_block`, `update_block`. The `discourse` server is read-only. <roam uid="Tf4JXJyRu"/>
    - **Read the publication behind an `@source`** → check its `metadata::` / `Abstract::` block first; for full text use the `zotero` MCP (`mcp__zotero__*`) when it's in the user's Zotero library. <roam uid="wsMfcY8Rf"/>
    - **Find who created a block** → `mcp__roam__datalog_query` on `:create/user`. There is no dedicated block-author tool on either MCP server; this query is the only reliable way to get block-level provenance. Always bind it to a page or a uid — unbounded, it returns every block in the graph. <roam uid="YemilM2pX" refs="1"/>
      - By page: `[:find ?uid ?creator ?editor :in $ ?page-title :where [?p :node/title ?page-title] [?b :block/page ?p] [?b :block/uid ?uid] [?b :create/user ?cu] [?cu :user/display-page ?cp] [?cp :node/title ?creator] [?b :edit/user ?eu] [?eu :user/display-page ?ep] [?ep :node/title ?editor]]` — returns uid + names only. Don't add `?b :block/string ?s` unless you need it: it re-returns the whole page you already read, roughly 7x the tokens. <roam uid="7BKClr9BK" refs="1"/>
      - For a single block, replace the two page clauses with `[?b :block/uid ?uid]` and pass the uid as the input. <roam uid="icLRn-ci0" refs="1"/>
    - **Find who created a page or discourse node** → `mcp__discourse__get_node uid=…` returns `author`, `author_uid`, `created`, `modified`. Page-level only — given a __block__ uid it returns the content with no author, so fall back to the datalog query above. <roam uid="wRmrVnFqO" refs="1"/>
    - **List every identity in the graph** → `mcp__discourse__get_users` — humans, bots, and API tokens with their uids. Resolve a partial name here before making any authorship claim. <roam uid="7IXa9Yq2g" refs="1"/>
    - **See what one person wrote recently** → `mcp__discourse__catch_me_up author="…" days=N`. Needs the exact display name from `get_users`. <roam uid="0gEBMNuKz" refs="1"/>
    - **Find the discourse nodes a person authored** → `mcp__discourse__get_researcher_contributions author="…"`. Node __pages__ only — it returns 0 for identities that write blocks but never create node pages, so a 0 is not evidence that someone wrote nothing. <roam uid="0OshhlAu4" refs="1"/>
    - **Filter an existing query by author** → `mcp__discourse__run_discourse_query query_uid=…` honors the query builder's `created by` / `edited by` conditions. <roam uid="MyIALn-lG" refs="1"/>
    - On every call, pass the graph explicitly (`graph="dg-team"`) — several graphs are configured, and the wrong one silently returns nothing. <roam uid="STWu7JWy_"/>
  - Entry point <roam uid="MHzuk97bt" heading="3"/>
    - Start from [[🚪 Discourse graphs front page for team members]], which orients you to the main dashboards, functions/flows, pilot status, and hypotheses/results. <roam uid="nPt2-iVnj"/>
  - Following page references for context <roam uid="h9NTRhMjK" heading="3"/>
    - Much of a node's meaning lives in its **page references** — the `[[double-bracketed]]` links within its content blocks. These connect nodes to the Functions, Flows, Projects, Sources, and UserPilots that give them context. <roam uid="U28zLlsXL"/>
    - When reading a node, expand or follow its page references to understand **why** it exists and **what** it connects to. For example, a Result node's title includes its Source (e.g., `[[RES]] - users synthesized 3x more claims - [[@pilotStudy2025]]`), and its body may reference the Function or Flow it relates to. <roam uid="BQMJ8e_-z"/>
    - **Linked references** (at the bottom of any page) show every block in the graph that mentions that page. This is the primary way to see how a node is used in context — meeting notes, update logs, other discourse nodes, and daily notes entries. <roam uid="G9z0oYOKm"/>
    - **Block references** work similarly for individual blocks (bullets). If a block has a reference count, it has been cited elsewhere. <roam uid="Dcv_AHP0W"/>
  - Search strategies <roam uid="uDgL2s89Q" heading="3"/>
    - Search for discourse nodes by their type prefix: `[[QUE]] -`, `[[ISS]] -`, `[[FLO]] -`, `[[RES]] -`, etc. <roam uid="z9FqVtbYA"/>
    - Search for candidate nodes by their tag: `#iss-candidate`, `#res-candidate`, `#hyp-candidate`, `#clm-candidate`, `#flow-candidate`, `#up-candidate`, `#pro-candidate`. <roam uid="R6ZQgo7E-"/>
    - Search with empty query to see recently edited and viewed content — useful for understanding current activity. <roam uid="aHXgbk2iE"/>
    - For attributes with constrained values (status fields, priorities, tools, etc.), refer to [[roam/js/attribute-select]] for the canonical set of options. <roam uid="MaJPh5WXZ"/>
  - Understanding overall workflows <roam uid="3Qe0kZwzj" heading="3"/>
    - An observation from a pilot (Result) often triggers an idea for improvement (Issue). Issues are higher priority when they improve an important Flow, which in turn enables a key Function. Once engineering works on an issue, it becomes a feature (Artifact). <roam uid="E-6z55uoF"/>
    - Result → Issue → Flow → Function → Artifact traces the path from observation to shipped feature. <roam uid="gFNP0A0S9"/>
- Writing into the graph <roam uid="a7uWA6zlm" heading="2"/>
  - Leave node creation and tagging to the team by default (see **Agent Behavior → General rules** below). When you are explicitly asked to capture something — a candidate node, a pilot observation, a flow — follow these conventions so each block reads cleanly now **and** is trivial to promote into a formal discourse node later. <roam uid="mebOIP95I"/>
  - Put each concept in its own block <roam uid="F3EVfNmD7" heading="3"/>
    - Write one idea — one claim, observation, pain point, flow, or action — per block. Don't pack several into a single bullet. Be parsimonious with any commentary you consider adding. <roam uid="1LMq1Ui6Y"/>
      - Atomic blocks are individually addressable: each can be block-referenced (`((uid))`), tagged, and promoted to a node on its own. A compound bullet can't. <roam uid="rLZacptHP"/>
    - Use indentation to carry structure: the parent block states the idea; child blocks hold its detail, caveats, steps, and references. <roam uid="VFcltIeP4"/>
      - This mirrors a discourse node, where the title is the idea and the template sections are the children. <roam uid="dv7_tHNg5"/>
  - Make candidate blocks formalizable <roam uid="t62zcsYxS" heading="3"/>
    - When you tag a block with a candidate tag, write the statement so it can become the node's **title almost verbatim** — the eventual node title should be roughly the same words as the block. Keep it atomic and self-contained: understandable without the surrounding meeting / log context. <roam uid="QcHWU8FCu"/>
    - Match the target node's title grammar so promotion is mechanical. The candidate tags in use here are `#iss-candidate`, `#res-candidate`, `#hyp-candidate`, `#clm-candidate`, `#flow-candidate`, `#up-candidate`, `#pro-candidate` — each maps to the node type of the same prefix (see **Graph Ontology** above for every format). Common cases: <roam uid="vNFJ3JbII"/>
      - `#res-candidate` → a discrete, past-tense pilot observation → `[[RES]] - {statement} - {Source}`. Name the `@source` / UserPilot in a child so it can be appended to the title on promotion. <roam uid="Xx5QnpXMw"/>
        - Example: `Pilot users created 3x more claims after the canvas node preview shipped #res-candidate` <roam uid="8RsFzOBwL"/>
      - `#iss-candidate` → an actionable dev or research item → `[[ISS]] - {statement}`. <roam uid="0tM9FtTCr"/>
        - Example: `Group nodes on the canvas by semantic similarity #iss-candidate` <roam uid="b8CJepmiH"/>
      - `#flow-candidate` → a tool-specific interaction flow → `[[FLO]] - {statement}`. <roam uid="alG4QCDR4"/>
        - Example: `Preview / view DG node info while on the tldraw canvas #flow-candidate` <roam uid="skG-2mzeZ"/>
    - If you can't yet phrase an idea atomically, leave it as plain text and don't tag it — a vague stub can't be promoted without a rewrite. <roam uid="znTpKgzZv"/>
  - Put supporting context in child blocks <roam uid="YE6FUcUKB" heading="3"/>
    - Everything that explains, grounds, or qualifies a candidate goes in **child blocks beneath it, never crammed into the statement**.  On promotion these children carry over into the node's template sections. <roam uid="VwHNAB0ij"/>
    - `#res-candidate` → Source + method + a screenshot or Loom → **Grounding Context** and **Snippets**. `#flow-candidate` → **Description** (Goal, Loom), **Steps**, **Pain points**. `#iss-candidate` → why it matters + the Flow / Function it improves → Issue Status / Type / Project / Flow properties. <roam uid="-zzjS0GNH"/>
    - Link related nodes with `[[…]]` inside the children — those page references become the node's discourse connections (Supports / Opposes / Informs / Resolves) once it is formalized. <roam uid="pM5ojIoXO"/>
  - Reuse the existing syntax and formatting conventions <roam uid="MEWdJCUaQ" heading="3"/>
    - For how to __reference__ nodes when writing (Roam alias syntax, `((uid))`), follow **Agent Behavior → Citing and referencing nodes** below — don't paste full URLs inside Roam. <roam uid="iqnB7VJ1X"/>
    - For callouts, colors, and foldable blocks, use the palette documented in **Agent Behavior → Formatting** below. <roam uid="1-PwVXvKX"/>
    - Reference only node titles you have actually found in the graph; never fabricate one. Preserve node title regex formats exactly (`[[RES]] - … - {Source}`, `[[FLO]] - …`, `UserPilot/…`) — a malformed title silently drops the block out of the discourse graph. <roam uid="ldsx0Q1Nj"/>
- Agent Behavior <roam uid="HQkVaTtF9" heading="2"/>
  - Information hierarchy <roam uid="Omx-xxku_" heading="3"/>
    - **Prioritize formalized node pages** (full `[[TYPE]] - title` pages with templates filled in). These represent the team's vetted, structured knowledge. <roam uid="gSd5Imn_Z"/>
    - **Then candidate nodes** (`#type-candidate` tagged blocks). These are preliminary but intentionally captured ideas. <roam uid="KPWTNgy6Z"/>
    - **Then remaining content** (meeting notes, daily notes, log entries, comments). These provide context but are less curated. <roam uid="7FBUcDopw"/>
    - Rank by formality, but check authorship before you cite — only human-written blocks are citable. See **Synthesize human content, not agent content** below. <roam uid="RgZPUYxXj" refs="1"/>
  - Synthesize human content, not agent content <roam uid="IxsMpHOOT" heading="3" refs="1"/>
    - **Your job is synthesis of what the team's people wrote.**  Building on agent-authored content closes a loop where agents cite agents and the graph fills with its own echo. <roam uid="2vCRnvaM-" refs="1"/>
    - **This includes your own prior output.** Never cite, quote, count, or treat as evidence a block that you or another agent wrote, in this graph or any other. <roam uid="r-7VcjnUB" refs="1"/>
  - Provenance: who wrote this block <roam uid="psNqP1Ow4" heading="3" refs="1"/>
    - **Never ascribe a statement to a person without querying the block's creator.** Position in the outline, a nearby name, and a `#[[Name]]` tag are not authorship signals — a person tag usually marks an assignee or a mention, and meeting notes are typed by one scribe on everyone's behalf. Look up `:create/user` before writing "X thinks", "per Joel", or any attributed quote. <roam uid="QowkWQTjg" refs="1"/>
    - **When creator and last editor differ, report both.** "Created by `matt-AI-bot`, last edited by Karola Kirsanow" is the honest form. Don't collapse it to one name. <roam uid="ABeXcABpE" refs="1"/>
    - **Speaker initials in meeting notes are the exception, and you should honor them.** On `Sync /` pages, `JC:`, `MAP:`, `MG:`, `KK:`, `MA:` are the scribe's record of who spoke. Attribute the __position__ to the initials and the __block__ to its creator, and say the initials are your basis. <roam uid="zgFhSiYI6" refs="1"/>
    - **If you can't resolve authorship, say the block is unattributed.** Never assign it to the nearest name on the page. <roam uid="CFgMF_i0-" refs="1"/>
    - **Non-human identities in this graph today:** `matt-AI-bot`, `ai-cybrarian`, `cybrarian-ai`, `Michael Gartner (AI)`, and every identity whose display name begins with `API Token:` or `Local API Token:`. Treat those as machine-written unless you have checked otherwise. Per-bot users are still being sorted out — see [[Convention/Human-AI interaction in Roam]]. <roam uid="78YnS6gEC" refs="1"/>
      - A token is not automatically an agent. `API Token: Raycast matt` and `API Token: send2graph` forward text a human typed. Token-created means __provenance unclear__, not __AI-generated__ — report which one you actually found. <roam uid="VBVOklCV1" refs="1"/>
      - `Discourse Graphs`, `Anonymous`, and `Anonymous_1`–`Anonymous_3` are shared or unresolved accounts. Don't attribute their blocks to any individual. <roam uid="rHnvdFRhH" refs="1"/>
    - **You may read agent content as context, but don't cite it.** Use an agent-written summary or digest to locate the human blocks underneath, then read and cite those. Consider the agent-written content as background context, not citable material. <roam uid="tCRWvyruf" refs="1"/>
    - **When the human record is thin, say so.** If the only coverage of a topic is agent-written, report that the team has not covered it rather than laundering an agent's take into a finding. <roam uid="PDwgHjakx" refs="1"/>
  - Citing and referencing nodes <roam uid="1Q-QuB4hm" heading="3"/>
    - When referencing discourse nodes in your responses, use **Roam alias syntax** so the link is readable but navigable: <roam uid="iZecLmaRZ"/>
      - `[the claim about synthesis]([[[[CLM]] - discourse graphs improve synthesis]])` <roam uid="-XCMrdIIk"/>
      - `[this pilot result]([[[[RES]] - users synthesized 3x more claims - [[@pilotStudy2025]]]]])` <roam uid="47VfBEfiy"/>
      - `[canvas node preview flow]([[[[FLO]] - Preview/view DG node info while on canvas]])` <roam uid="9VQN1PcbM"/>
      - `[the grouping issue]([[[[ISS]] - group nodes on the canvas, eg by semantic similarity]])` <roam uid="huKrbfYiZ"/>
    - For block-level references, use the `((uid))` syntax when you have a specific block UID. <roam uid="P03iIKmxK"/>
    - Always include enough of the node title for the reader to understand the reference without clicking through. <roam uid="6rl43A8ym"/>
  - Citing dates <roam uid="FNMHIgv1c" heading="3"/>
    - The team uses the linked references of daily notes pages as a "table of contents" to monitor the team's work that week. Therefore, be judicious in how many times you reference a daily note with wikilinks. The top-level entry usually includes a reference to today's date, and any clear deadline can be referenced once per entry. Other dates should be labeled like `July 29` rather than with wikilinks. <roam uid="AJ-MJrH7M"/>
  - Reading nodes thoroughly <roam uid="UJfOc9mSn" heading="3"/>
    - When investigating a node, don't stop at the title. Read the template sections (Summary, Description, Rationale, etc.) for substance, and follow page references in the content for context. <roam uid="9mWl4_KbG"/>
    - All the firebase links are public links to images.  Usually, these images are very informative, so for relevant nodes and pages you should open the images and interpret them with your image recognition capabilities <roam uid="EIquKiNkw"/>
    - Check linked references to see where the node has been discussed in meetings, logs, and other nodes. <roam uid="rsCUVEZGn"/>
    - For Results and Evidence, pay attention to the Source in the title and the Grounding Context section for methodological detail. <roam uid="rxcu3DrEs"/>
  - Linking to this graph <roam uid="sTxa7aNev" heading="3"/>
    - If you create a URL in the agentic chat UI (outside of roam), remember that the URL starts with `https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/`. The graph url is discourse-graphs; the graph MCP nickname is dg-team. <roam uid="8VfrwIAkz"/>
  - Formatting <roam uid="DLi8zMdfk" heading="3"/>
    - When writing in Roam, you can make use of colors, color underlines, and comments: <roam uid="UPWoTfgXC"/>
      - [[>]] [[!NOTE]] This is a basic note callout\nNotes are great for highlighting general information you want to draw attention to. <roam uid="GRXCvlZXR"/>
      - [[>]] [[!INFO]] Informational callout with an info icon\nUse these for additional context or background details. <roam uid="q9AGKeYbe"/>
      - [[>]] [[!SUMMARY]] A summary or abstract callout\nPerfect for executive summaries, TLDRs, or condensed overviews. <roam uid="-e0ZjrNmx"/>
      - [[>]] [[!TIP]] Helpful tip — try using callouts for emphasis!\nCombine callouts with **bold**, *italic*, and `code` formatting in both the title and body. <roam uid="QZj72rl96"/>
      - [[>]] [[!SUCCESS]] Operation completed successfully\nAll 47 tests passed. The deployment to staging is live. <roam uid="qnaPlXY2m"/>

- Require editor access to a space before adding accounts to it #iss-candidate <roam uid="5cTXWhzAt" heading="1" refs="6"/>
  - Need / Problem Statement <roam uid="1jHL1QXBq"/>
    - What is the problem that you are trying to solve? <roam uid="f5EqE3XRJ"/>
      - The problem is: any logged-in user can give themselves `editor` access to any other space on the same platform. They call the `upsert_account_in_space` function with that space's id and their own account. Nothing checks that they have access to the space. <roam uid="q4a8xotgj"/>
      - `upsert_account_in_space` (`supabase/schemas/account.sql`) adds an account to a space. It upserts the `PlatformAccount` row and adds `LocalAccess` and `AgentIdentifier` rows. If the account has an owner (`dg_account`), it also adds a `SpaceAccess` row for that owner. It is `SECURITY DEFINER`, so it skips row-level security on all four tables. <roam uid="p_A8BRYXP"/>
      - The only limit on the new `SpaceAccess` row is `least(my_permissions_in_space(space_id_), 'editor')`. `my_permissions_in_space` returns NULL when the caller has no access to the space. Postgres's `LEAST` ignores NULL arguments, so the result is `editor`. <roam uid="O3CGol4HA"/>
      - `create_account_in_space` and `upsert_accounts_in_space` call it and have the same problem. <roam uid="8qkwPVtqD"/>
    - Who is affected? What are they trying to do, and what is stopping them? <roam uid="6XQKf7rHx"/>
      - Every space. An attacker with editor access can read and change all of the space's content and accounts. <roam uid="MFiGcL_Ze"/>
      - The attack: <roam uid="Z9QEZ_OFc"/>
        - 1. The attacker logs in as an account they own. The simplest is the anonymous account of a space they created: `create-space` gives it `dg_account` = its own auth user and `account_local_id` = the space's email, which the attacker's plugin already knows. A person account with an owner also works. <roam uid="hAWy9Ujy_"/>
        - 2. The attacker picks a target space id on the same platform. Space ids come from the shared `entity_id_seq` sequence, so they can be enumerated. <roam uid="SJ-eekUfg"/>
        - 3. The attacker calls `rpc("upsert_account_in_space", { space_id_: <target>, local_account: { account_local_id: <their own> } })`. <roam uid="gL-Y1Ezhe"/>
        - 4. The function reads the target space's platform. `ON CONFLICT (account_local_id, platform)` matches the attacker's own account and returns its `dg_account`. <roam uid="WoN6ob550"/>
        - 5. The function inserts `SpaceAccess(<target>, <attacker's uid>, 'editor')`. <roam uid="P1tzv7kiT"/>
        - 6. The attacker now has editor access to the target space through the normal policies and views. <roam uid="B5lMOZzQN"/>
      - Without step 1, any caller can still change other accounts: rename any `PlatformAccount` by its `account_local_id`, link any account to any space through `LocalAccess`, and add email identifiers to any account. <roam uid="s1rl-kfut"/>
    - What request, observation, or other evidence supports this? <roam uid="qXJamvajG"/>
      - Found by reading the schema while documenting the Supabase security warnings ([[[[Supabase]] Warnings]], ENG-2436). The full attack has not been reproduced. <roam uid="SencBB3i9"/>
      - Verified on the local test database: `anon` and `authenticated` both have EXECUTE on `upsert_account_in_space`, `upsert_accounts_in_space` and `create_account_in_space` (`has_function_privilege`). <roam uid="yWpYe1ngO"/>
      - Verified on the local test database: `SELECT least(NULL::text, 'editor')` returns `editor`. <roam uid="aiAPch8cs"/>
      - Steps 1, 4 and 5 come from reading `create-space/index.ts` and `upsert_account_in_space`. Step 2 comes from `space.sql`, where `Space.id` defaults to `nextval('entity_id_seq')`. <roam uid="1jrvCd-wV"/>
  - Proposed approach <roam uid="_rfvyEhhv"/>
    - At the start of `upsert_account_in_space`, raise an error unless the caller has `editor` access to the space (`my_permissions_in_space(space_id_) >= 'editor'`). The function then no longer needs `least` to cap the permission at the caller's level; if it keeps it, add a `COALESCE`. <roam uid="USJCDt3UF"/>
    - Check the internal callers. The document and content upsert functions in `content.sql` and `concept.sql` call `create_account_in_space` and `upsert_account_in_space` for authors. They should already require editor access to the same space; confirm that, so the new check doesn't break sync. <roam uid="k5mSKPV_Q"/>
    - Revoke EXECUTE on the three functions from `anon`. Plugins call `create_account_in_space` only after logging in (`fetchOrCreatePlatformAccount` in `contextFunctions.ts`). <roam uid="MEpLr1CtL"/>
    - Add cucumber scenarios: a user with no access to a space, and a user with reader access, both fail to add an account to it and get no `SpaceAccess` row. <roam uid="3DgnWQOdm"/>
    - After the fix, check production for `SpaceAccess` rows that this path could have created: an `editor` row for an anonymous space account on a space that isn't its own. <roam uid="8h_eDTmfJ"/>
  - Fit and urgency <roam uid="zEOCuqwG4"/>
    - ^^What accepted user, developer, or project need would this address?^^ <roam uid="atwji8viB"/>
      - Only people the space has granted access to can read or change its content. <roam uid="GEtUqTB0-"/>
    - Is it relevant to work expected within the next six months? <roam uid="5pTTI9QON"/>
      - Yes. Group sharing, cross-space import and public nodes all depend on `SpaceAccess` being trustworthy. <roam uid="XHfbNFs-T"/>
    - Why consider it now? What happens if we delay it? <roam uid="kscaZoyg2"/>
      - The fix is a few lines in one function. Until it ships, any logged-in plugin user can take editor access to any other space on their platform. <roam uid="EVCUKfDHe"/>
  - Triage <roam uid="Pw5B9Tg7P"/>
    - Is the need clear enough to create an engineering ticket? <roam uid="dsxkCsvsV"/>
    - Outcome: Ready for engineering ticket / Explore / Park / Reject <roam uid="ThhUWOuuQ"/>
    - Reason: <roam uid="ITWqtjK2C"/>
- Stop signed-in users from joining another user's space access through a self-created group membership #iss-candidate <roam uid="Wwm8OO2uF" heading="1" refs="3"/>
  - Need / Problem Statement <roam uid="zhUB8Yr6X"/>
    - What is the problem that you are trying to solve? <roam uid="BWtfY1N3P"/>
      - The problem is: any signed-in user can add themselves as a member of a "group" whose ID is another user's ID, and then gets every space that user can access, up to editor. <roam uid="XNAzHpGh0"/>
      - Background: space access is granted per user ID in the `SpaceAccess` table. A group is a user account whose ID others can hold through a row in `group_membership`. The access check `my_user_accounts()` returns your own user ID plus every group ID you are a member of, so a group's space access becomes yours. `in_space`, `my_space_ids` and `can_access_account` all rely on it. <roam uid="489JZGJAv"/>
      - Cause: the row-level security rule for inserting into `group_membership` is `is_group_admin(group_id) OR NOT group_exists(group_id)`. The second half was meant to let the first member create a new group. `group_exists` only checks whether any membership row already uses that group ID. An ordinary person's user ID has never been used as a group ID, so the check passes for it. The `group_id` column only requires an existing user ID, so any user ID is accepted. <roam uid="-URaf7wck"/>
      - Attack steps, as read from the schema (not yet reproduced against a database): <roam uid="TvfIzQcMf"/>
        - 1. Attacker A and user B both belong to space S1. B also has access to space S2, which A does not. <roam uid="59HcuyfiW"/>
        - 2. A reads B's user ID from `PlatformAccount.dg_account`. The select rule on `PlatformAccount` allows this for accounts in a shared space. <roam uid="UlSJhdINp"/>
        - 3. A inserts a `group_membership` row with `member_id` set to A and `group_id` set to B's user ID. `group_exists` returns false, so the insert is allowed. The `admin` column defaults to true. <roam uid="-SCE51d-h"/>
        - 4. `my_user_accounts()` now returns B's user ID for A, so A gets B's access level on S2, including editor. <roam uid="yw8jVkapB"/>
      - The same rule also lets anyone take over a real group after its last member leaves, since members can delete their own membership row. A space's anonymous user is also claimable if its user ID is known; space members can read it from `PlatformAccount`. <roam uid="B9b-1zYBp"/>
    - Who is affected? What are they trying to do, and what is stopping them? <roam uid="Bw-8tmKbL"/>
      - Every user of a shared space. They rely on space access to decide who can read and edit their content, and this rule lets a user outside the space bypass it. <roam uid="KXJ06WsBf"/>
    - What request, observation, or other evidence supports this? <roam uid="maUYdjZbp"/>
      - A bug report stated that an ordinary signed-in account can gain access to a space it was never given. The report did not include the mechanism. <roam uid="UnYIEEqZ3"/>
      - The rule is in `packages/database/supabase/schemas/account.sql` (`group_membership_insert_policy`) and was deployed by the migration `20260101183250_group_access.sql`. <roam uid="u7qePBCL0"/>
      - The Cucumber step that adds a space's anonymous user to a group (in `features/step-definitions/stepdefs.ts`) reads that user ID from `PlatformAccount` by its predictable email, which confirms step 2. <roam uid="GvE4PACDo"/>
  - Fit and urgency <roam uid="0upFljshr"/>
    - ^^What accepted user, developer, or project need would this address?^^ <roam uid="jOS9RYOLa"/>
      - Space access control must hold for shared spaces. Today any signed-in user who shares one space with someone can reach all of that person's other spaces. <roam uid="kqcIrtVff"/>
    - Is it relevant to work expected within the next six months? <roam uid="OBrzfLNqm"/>
      - Yes. Group and space sharing are in active use, and the hole is open in the deployed schema. <roam uid="bGQfZAJx3"/>
    - Why consider it now? What happens if we delay it? <roam uid="xClnu2Apc"/>
      - It is an access control bypass with a reported symptom. While it stays open, any shared space can be read or edited by users it was never shared with. <roam uid="afyfAjahx"/>
  - Triage <roam uid="HMylN9JuX"/>
    - Is the need clear enough to create an engineering ticket? <roam uid="m41iunM41"/>
      - Yes. A likely fix is small: drop the `NOT group_exists(group_id)` clause so the rule becomes `is_group_admin(group_id)`. <roam uid="AGHOXoYZl"/>
      - Nothing depends on that clause. Groups are created by the `create-group` edge function, which inserts the first membership with the service role and so bypasses row-level security. Joining by invitation goes through `accept_group_invitation`, which runs as a security definer. The only direct client insert is a group admin adding a member in the Cucumber steps, and it passes `is_group_admin`. <roam uid="CAFUACCx3"/>
      - The ticket should include a test that reproduces steps 1 to 4 before the fix and fails after it. <roam uid="7NhjZRi1Z"/>
    - Outcome: Ready for engineering ticket <roam uid="ZFW1oN1Qm"/>
    - Reason: the mechanism is identified in the schema, the fix is one rule change, and no existing code path needs the clause being removed. <roam uid="KK4cRjNKg"/>
- Restrict claiming an unowned account to a logged-in person claiming a person account #iss-candidate <roam uid="vtxvgZEKp" heading="1" refs="2"/>
  - {{[[TODO]]}} [[+Sid]] I think this is the issue that your Claude found. <roam uid="s4FutlyXI"/>
  - Need / Problem Statement <roam uid="5HgJOytp0"/>
    - What is the problem that you are trying to solve? <roam uid="hTEvW2Hop"/>
      - The problem is: any client with editor access to a space can claim that space's unowned accounts, by setting their `dg_account` to its own auth user. That includes the space's anonymous account, which every plugin client of the space logs in as. Claiming should be limited to a person, logged in as themselves, claiming a person account. <roam uid="V0MG_ma5o"/>
      - The `PlatformAccount` insert, update and delete policies allow a write when `dg_account = auth.uid()`, or when `dg_account IS NULL` and `unowned_account_in_shared_space(id, 'editor')` is true. That function (`supabase/schemas/account.sql`) checks that the current user has editor access, directly or through a group, to a space where the account has `LocalAccess`. It checks neither the account's `agent_type` nor who the current user is. <roam uid="DPGCYWuhS"/>
    - Who is affected? What are they trying to do, and what is stopping them? <roam uid="piHkyWSeo"/>
      - Person accounts, such as the authors listed in a Roam graph. Today they have no owner until claimed. Anyone using a space's plugin, or any member of a group with editor access to the space, can claim them. The claimant then owns the account under the `PlatformAccount` policies: it can update the account and delete it. `Document.author_id` cascades on delete. <roam uid="3fry6v7W3"/>
      - When person logins exist, the intended flow is presumably that a person claims their own account. An earlier claim by someone else would block that. <roam uid="Nwi4gQxIB"/>
      - Anonymous accounts get their `dg_account` when the space is created (`supabase/functions/create-space/index.ts`), so the "claimed account must be a person" half changes nothing today. It guards against an anonymous account that was ever left without an owner. <roam uid="dPt419ImU"/>
    - What request, observation, or other evidence supports this? <roam uid="tp2lpjWnY"/>
      - Found while testing the updatable-views issue candidate from [[ENG-2344]]. On the local test database, logged in through the real auth and PostgREST endpoints as space s2's anonymous account, `PATCH /rest/v1/PlatformAccount?dg_account=is.null` claimed s2's own unowned person account `user2`. The policy allows this as written. Verified. <roam uid="fJsj15uTJ"/>
      - Supabase's `auth.users.is_anonymous` is `false` for our space accounts, which sign in with email and password. It cannot tell a space account from a person. Verified on the local test database. <roam uid="Gd61Kpj6v"/>
  - Proposed approach <roam uid="fFISLryEt"/>
    - Add `pa.agent_type = 'person'` to the account condition in `unowned_account_in_shared_space`. <roam uid="7kewfqOmb"/>
    - Require the current user not to be a space account: no `PlatformAccount` with `dg_account = auth.uid()` and `agent_type = 'anonymous'`. The check must look at `auth.uid()` itself, not at the group through which the editor access comes. <roam uid="ARgkaT6D8"/>
    - No client seems to claim accounts by update today. In `apps/*/src`, `apps/website/app` and `packages/*/src`, the only code that writes `dg_account` is the website's `POST /api/supabase/platform-account`, which inserts a new account or returns the existing one through `getOrCreateEntity`. The insert policy uses the same function, so the change also restricts that route; check that its callers only insert their own person account. <roam uid="yaYzcFYr-"/>
  - Fit and urgency <roam uid="qWgxI3FSx"/>
    - ^^What accepted user, developer, or project need would this address?^^ <roam uid="A1wztk9NL"/>
      - A person account should belong to the person it represents. <roam uid="UOrRQfQwZ"/>
    - Is it relevant to work expected within the next six months? <roam uid="9KozgpXRY"/>
      - When person logins are built. <roam uid="AzMDQ3YJt"/>
    - Why consider it now? What happens if we delay it? <roam uid="4ZdvBg-JA"/>
      - Less urgent than the updatable views. It matters once person accounts carry meaning or permissions, and claims made before then would have to be audited. <roam uid="w_QLYkQzO"/>
  - Triage <roam uid="xwDZuvdf3"/>
    - Is the need clear enough to create an engineering ticket? <roam uid="tDGe_-PRV"/>
    - Outcome: Ready for engineering ticket / Explore / Park / Reject <roam uid="8FwIdVzuS"/>
    - Reason: <roam uid="0jItxj5cG"/>
- Remove the unused dg_account and metadata columns from the my_accounts view #iss-candidate <roam uid="-SNrs-Lj_" heading="1" refs="1"/>
  - This is a smaller issue, but still real, and it leaks the information necessary for the previous attack. <roam uid="k6O7qJDLB"/>
  - Need / Problem Statement <roam uid="EHoYTSwDs"/>
    - What is the problem that you are trying to solve? <roam uid="8isc4D7QC"/>
      - The problem is: `my_accounts` shows every space peer the Supabase auth uid (`dg_account`) and the `metadata` of every account in the spaces they share, and no code uses either column. <roam uid="M2GE5okmK"/>
      - `my_accounts` lists every `PlatformAccount` with a `LocalAccess` row in a space where the caller has at least `partial` access, plus the caller's own accounts. <roam uid="JeKlaOP_p"/>
      - The view is not `security_invoker`, so it runs as its owner and skips the row-level security on `PlatformAccount`. What it returns is decided by its own filter. <roam uid="v60XoYuXX"/>
    - Who is affected? What are they trying to do, and what is stopping them? <roam uid="Q9fUX-Ruy"/>
      - Every account in a shared space. A peer with `partial` access in one space can read the auth uids of everyone in it, including the space's anonymous account. <roam uid="OZc0YLfiw"/>
      - Auth uids are not secrets by design, but some checks treat knowing one as enough. The group-membership hole (separate issue candidate) is one: it only needs a uid to take over someone's access. A space's anonymous account holds `editor` on its space, so its uid is the most valuable target. <roam uid="vuKCggxkW"/>
    - What request, observation, or other evidence supports this? <roam uid="cRtAiakMM"/>
      - Found by reading the schema during a security review. Not reproduced against a database. <roam uid="l2QggUzty"/>
      - No code reads `dg_account` or `metadata` from `my_accounts`. The only readers are Obsidian's `fetchUserNames` (`id`, `name`) and `getAccountMap` plus the author embeds in `packages/database/src/lib/queries.ts` (`id`, `account_local_id`). <roam uid="OEllPfhKj"/>
      - Code that needs `dg_account` reads it elsewhere: the website's `account.ts` filters `PlatformAccount` on the caller's own uid, group management reads `my_pseudo_accounts`, and the cucumber steps use the service client. <roam uid="LP-aPT3fA"/>
  - Fit and urgency <roam uid="6ZNpl8tak"/>
    - ^^What accepted user, developer, or project need would this address?^^ <roam uid="I71XX8Tgo"/>
      - Expose only the account fields that clients use. <roam uid="PuPcO-XmU"/>
    - Is it relevant to work expected within the next six months? <roam uid="hHdWOzFPw"/>
      - Yes. Any change that widens who can read `my_accounts` widens the uid exposure with it. <roam uid="sFjs4udPM"/>
    - Why consider it now? What happens if we delay it? <roam uid="HA6BdryaB"/>
      - The change is small while the view has two readers. Until it ships, auth uids reach anyone who shares a space with their owner. <roam uid="-bkfLplO5"/>
  - Triage <roam uid="amHHh7zea"/>
    - Is the need clear enough to create an engineering ticket? <roam uid="HPM3OmUUv"/>
      - Proposed scope: drop `dg_account` and `metadata` from `my_accounts`. <roam uid="bcufJ-PfZ"/>
      - `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` cannot remove columns, so the view needs `DROP VIEW` and `CREATE VIEW`. `author_of_content` and `author_of_concept` return `SETOF public.my_accounts`, so they need dropping and recreating too. <roam uid="QBvV_uzTh"/>
      - `dbTypes` then needs regenerating from a fresh database. <roam uid="XlCHvLsZJ"/>
    - Outcome: Ready for engineering ticket / Explore / Park / Reject <roam uid="V6c2-3WDn"/>
    - Reason: <roam uid="37kiMG1v3"/>
- Stop asset readers from overwriting asset files #iss-candidate <roam uid="jELOBilLa" heading="1" refs="1"/>
  - Independently found, worth working on. And it's tiny. <roam uid="dDHipD1Zu"/>
  - Need / Problem Statement <roam uid="_VGh6qx0-"/>
    - What is the problem that you are trying to solve? <roam uid="EcijgRqf7"/>
      - The problem is: any logged-in user can replace the bytes of any asset file they can read, even with read-only access to its space. <roam uid="BPYy_rC8B"/>

The dev stack runs under project id `test` (`supabase_db_test`), while `packages/database/supabase/config.toml` declares `discourse-graphs`, so the two collide. Do **not** `supabase stop --project-id test` — that kills his running dev stack. Skip the setup step instead: `./node_modules/.bin/tsc` then run cucumber directly against the stack that is already up. `.env.local` already points at `http://127.0.0.1:54321` and authenticates fine.
- Use `./node_modules/.bin/cucumber-js`, never `npx cucumber-js` — npx resolves it to a dependency-confusion placeholder published on the registry, which prints a scary "misconfiguration" banner and runs nothing.
- Prefix `PATH` with node lts/jod, see [[openspec-cli-location]], and pass `SUPABASE_USE_DB=local` (otherwise scripts report "Not using the database" and no-op).

A clean run is 18 scenarios / 184 steps, about 12 seconds.

**Re-check the target before every run, 2026-10-02 (ENG-2344).** Permission to run cucumber "on the test database" holds only while that database is the one on port 54322. They switch stacks mid-session: `supabase_db_test` and `supabase_db_discourse-graphs` both bind 54322. I ran the suite against `discourse-graphs` after they had switched to it for an EXPLAIN comparison, and they stopped me: "don't run cucumber on the non-test database!" The "database is blank" step failed on its first DELETE, a `file_gc` duplicate key, so the DELETE rolled back and no data was lost. That was luck.

**How to apply:** before each cucumber run, and before any DDL, run `docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep _db_` and proceed only if it shows `supabase_db_test`. Otherwise stop and ask.

I'm stopping before writing any code, because the first issue doesn't work the way the Roam page says. The escalation fails, but the function has a different, real hole.

**The editor escalation (attack steps 5–6) fails today.** When the account has an owner, `upsert_account_in_space` raises an error before it can insert `SpaceAccess`. There are two separate bugs in that branch:

- The `COALESCE(local_account.permissions, CASE … THEN 'editor' … END)` mixes `SpaceAccessPermissions` with `text`, so it fails with `COALESCE types public."SpaceAccessPermissions" and text cannot be matched`.
- Even with that fixed, `my_permissions_in_space` is called without the `public.` prefix while the function runs with `search_path = ''`. That raises `function my_permissions_in_space(...) does not exist`.

I reproduced both by calling the deployed function in a transaction I rolled back. The whole call aborts, so no `LocalAccess` or `SpaceAccess` row is written either. One more consequence: no legitimate caller can currently add an owned account to a space through these functions.

**What does work today:** anyone, including `anon`, can call it on any space id for an account with no owner. As `anon`, I renamed an unowned `PlatformAccount` and attached an email identifier to it in a rolled-back transaction. That's the "without step 1" paragraph on the Roam page, and it's live.

**This changes the fix.** If we only fix those two bugs, the editor escalation becomes real. So the fix has to do these together:

1. Raise unless `public.my_permissions_in_space(space_id_) >= 'editor'`, at the top of `upsert_account_in_space`. `upsert_accounts_in_space` and `create_account_in_space` both go through it.
2. Fix the `CASE` cast and qualify the call to `public.my_permissions_in_space`.
3. Revoke EXECUTE on the three functions from `anon`.
4. Check the internal callers in `content.sql` and `concept.sql`, and the two client callers: Roam's `upsertUsers` and `fetchOrCreatePlatformAccount`. Both run logged in as the space's account, which is an editor.
5. Add cucumber scenarios for a caller with no access and one with reader access, plus one where an owned account succeeds. Nothing tests that last case today, which is how the branch stayed broken.

The Roam issue candidate overstates the problem as written. I'd change the attack section to say steps 5–6 currently fail on the two bugs, and that fixing those without the check would open the hole. I haven't touched the page.

Note: the database on port 54322 is `supabase_db_discourse-graphs`, not `supabase_db_test`. I only ran statements inside transactions that I rolled back. Before any migration or cucumber run, I'll need you to switch to the test stack.

Should I go ahead with steps 1–5, and should I update the Roam page?
Hmm.. would you say that this looks like more than one issue now?

Yes, two. They're different kinds of problem, and one has to land before the other.

**1. Security: no access check (exploitable now).** Anyone, including `anon`, can rename an unowned account, link it to any space through `LocalAccess`, and attach email identifiers to it. The fix is the editor check plus revoking EXECUTE from `anon`. Its tests are a caller with no access and a caller with reader access trying to change an unowned account. This stands on its own and is what I'd do on the current branch.

**2. Bug: the owned-account branch always errors.** It has the `CASE`/`COALESCE` type mismatch and the unqualified `my_permissions_in_space`. It's a functional bug, not a security one. At the moment it actually blocks the escalation. It also has an ordering constraint: it must not ship before #1, or fixing it opens the editor escalation. So it should stack on #1. Its test is the one that's missing today: an owned account gets added to a space and gets the right `SpaceAccess` row.

Why #2 might wait, or might never be fixed as written: owned accounts barely exist yet. The space's anonymous account gets its `SpaceAccess` from `create-space` through the service role. Person logins aren't built yet, so nobody hits that branch today. That leaves a design question for when person logins are built: should adding a person's account to a space grant their auth user `SpaceAccess` at all? A claim, or an invitation, might be the right gate rather than an editor listing them as an author. That's a reason to file #2 as an issue candidate and decide then, rather than fix it now.

So my suggestion:

- Rewrite the current Roam candidate around #1 only: the unowned-account rewrite, which is reproduced. Mention the editor escalation only as what the bugs in #2 are currently blocking.
- Add a new candidate for #2 on the same page that says it depends on #1.
- On this branch, implement #1 only.

Do you want me to draft both Roam texts for you to review before I touch the page?
Yes, agreed on the separation.

# DG Engineering Writing Style

Write in a direct, concise, plainspoken style that preserves important context and qualification.

## Core style

- Lead with the relevant point and move quickly to the concrete question, request, or action.
- Prefer the shortest version that remains clear and preserves necessary nuance.
- Identify wording or missing context that is ambiguous or could be misconstrued. Resolve it when the intended meaning is clear; otherwise, flag it and ask for clarification.
- Use natural contractions and everyday wording. Avoid corporate jargon, inflated phrasing, and generic professional filler.
- Avoid em dashes as sentence-level punctuation. Use a period, comma, colon, semicolon, or parentheses to separate thoughts instead. Preserve em dashes only when they appear in exact quotations, titles, source text, or technical content supplied by the requester.
- When identifying a problem or disagreement, state it plainly and pivot toward clarification, resolution, criteria, or next steps.
- Prefer bullets for distinct points. When prose reads more naturally, keep paragraphs and sentences short; avoid run-on sentences.
- Ask one clear question when one will do. Combine related questions only when separating them would add needless length.

## Adapt to the channel

- For a quick reply or chat message, omit the greeting and sign-off when they add no value.
- For technical issues, describe the observed behavior, the relevant contrast or expectation, and the requested clarification or next step.
- For engineering tickets and technical documentation, apply these ASD-STE100-inspired principles:
  - Use one term consistently for each concept. Do not alternate between synonyms.
  - Put one primary action or idea in each sentence.
  - Prefer active voice when the actor is important.
  - Replace vague verbs such as "handle," "support," or "improve" with the specific behavior or result.

## Drafting rules

- Preserve facts, commitments, dates, names, links, and technical meaning supplied by the requester.
- Do not invent availability, decisions, commitments, or emotional language.
- Treat explicit directions such as "shorter," "warmer," "more forceful," "broader," or "one sentence" as overrides for the current draft.

      - `create_account_in_space` and `upsert_accounts_in_space` call it and have the same problem.
      - For an account without an owner, the caller can do three things: rename the `PlatformAccount`, link it to the space through `LocalAccess`, and add email identifiers to it.
      - For an account with an owner, the function currently fails with an error, so the call changes nothing. That failure is a separate bug (see the next issue candidate). Fixing that bug without this check would let a caller give editor access to any space to an account they own. The cap on the new `SpaceAccess` row, `least(my_permissions_in_space(space_id_), 'editor')`, does not stop this: `my_permissions_in_space` returns NULL when the caller has no access, and `LEAST` ignores NULL, so the result is `editor`.
    - Who is affected? What are they trying to do, and what is stopping them?
      - Every space with accounts that have no owner, which today includes most person accounts, such as the authors listed in a Roam graph. Their names and identifiers can be changed by anyone who knows their `account_local_id`.
    - What request, observation, or other evidence supports this?
      - Found by reading the schema while documenting the Supabase security warnings ([[[[Supabase]] Warnings]], ENG-2436).
      - Reproduced on a local database, in a transaction that was rolled back: as the `anon` role, `upsert_account_in_space` renamed an unowned `PlatformAccount` and added an email identifier to it.
      - Verified on the local test database: `anon` and `authenticated` both have EXECUTE on `upsert_account_in_space`, `upsert_accounts_in_space` and `create_account_in_space` (`has_function_privilege`).
      - Verified on the local test database: `SELECT least(NULL::text, 'editor')` returns `editor`.
  - Proposed approach
    - At the start of `upsert_account_in_space`, raise an error unless the caller has `editor` access to the space (`public.my_permissions_in_space(space_id_) >= 'editor'`).
    - Revoke EXECUTE on the three functions from `anon`. Plugins call `create_account_in_space` only after logging in (`fetchOrCreatePlatformAccount` in `contextFunctions.ts`).
    - Check the callers. The document and content upsert functions in `content.sql` and `concept.sql` call `create_account_in_space` and `upsert_account_in_space` for authors.       - Only people the space has granted access to can change its accounts.
    - Is it relevant to work expected within the next six months?

  - Triage

    - Reason:

A Linear ticket's description and its revision history are a collective document the team
reads. Do not make major changes to one with a direct edit. Describe the change first,
wait for explicit approval, and prefer recording substantial reasoning as a comment over
silently rewriting the body.

**Why:** teammates read the history to understand how a ticket's scope moved. A unilateral
rewrite erases that conversation and presents a conclusion no one agreed to. Said on
2026-09-10 after an unapproved rewrite of ENG-2219 that had to be reverted.

**How to apply:**
- General rule, stated 2026-09-27: never alter an existing ticket's body; add a comment
  instead. This covers small additions too. "Add a note in Linear" means a comment, not a
  new bullet under Notes (I put a bullet on ENG-2326 and had to move it to a comment).
  Creating a new ticket's description is the only exception.
- Relaxed 2026-09-29: a fresh ticket still in `Ticket Draft` (not yet approved) may be
  edited directly, especially to answer an open question it raised. Use a targeted patch.
  Once approved (moved to Triage, Backlog, Todo or later), the comment-only rule applies.
  First applied on ENG-2335, replacing its "Unverified dependency" note.
- "Now let me look at X" is a request to review, not approval. So is silence. Wait for a
  clear yes.
- When approved, use the smallest targeted patch, not a whole-description replacement, so
  the revision diff stays legible. `save_issue`'s `patch` operations do this.
- Once implementation settles a ticket's open question, do not even offer to "correct"
  the Solution or Notes to match. The decision goes in a comment; the body keeps the
  earlier wording so the ticket's evolution stays readable (ENG-2288, 2026-09-22).
- The same holds for any shared artifact with a history others read: PR bodies, specs,
  design docs. See [[git-operations-are-the-users]], which is the same principle for git
  state.

input.string: Those bugs are the only thing that stops a privilege escalation. If they were fixed, a caller could give an account they own editor access to any space. The cap on the new row, `least(my_permissions_in_space(space_id_), 'editor')`, does not stop this: `my_permissions_in_space` returns NULL when the caller has no access, and `LEAST` ignores NULL, so the result is `editor`.

input.markdown:
- For an account without an owner, the caller can do three things: rename the `PlatformAccount`, link it to the space through `LocalAccess`, and add email identifiers to it.
- For an account with an owner, the function currently fails with an error, so the call changes nothing. The branch that adds `SpaceAccess` has two bugs: a `COALESCE` that mixes `SpaceAccessPermissions` with `text`, and a call to `my_permissions_in_space` without the `public.` schema under `search_path = ''`.

- The branch should not exist. `LocalAccess` says that an account belongs to a space and gives no permission. `SpaceAccess` gives permission, and today only groups and a space's own account hold it. People will get `SpaceAccess` through their Discourse Graphs account, after the account verification planned for that. Granting it here, because an editor listed the person as an author, would bypass that verification.

Feature: Adding accounts to a space
  User story:
  * As a user of a plugin
  * Logged in through a given space's anonymous account
  * I can add the accounts of my space's authors to my space
  * But nobody without editor access to my space can change its accounts

  Acceptance criteria:
  * Clients that are not logged in cannot call the account functions
  * Users with no access or reader access to a space cannot add or rename accounts through it
  * Adding an account that has an owner gives that owner no access to the space

  Background:
    Given the database is blank
    And the user user1 opens the Roam plugin in space s1
    And the user user2 opens the Roam plugin in space s2

  Scenario: Clients that are not logged in cannot add accounts
    Then a client that is not logged in fails to upsert these accounts to space s1:
      """json
      [{ "account_local_id": "user1", "name": "renamed" }]
      """
    And the account user1 should be named "user1"

  Scenario: Users with no access to a space cannot add accounts to it
    Then user user2 fails to upsert these accounts to space s1:
      """json
      [
        { "account_local_id": "user1", "name": "renamed" },
        { "account_local_id": "intruder", "name": "intruder" }
      ]
      """
    And the account user1 should be named "user1"
    And a user logged in space s1 should see 2 PlatformAccount in the database

  Scenario: Users with reader access to a space cannot add accounts to it
    When user of space s1 creates group my_group
    And user of space s1 adds space s2 to group my_group
    And SpaceAccess are added to the database:
      | _account_uid | _space_id | permissions |
      | my_group     | s1        | reader      |
    Then user user2 fails to upsert these accounts to space s1:
      """json
      [
        { "account_local_id": "user1", "name": "renamed" },
        { "account_local_id": "intruder", "name": "intruder" }
      ]
      """
    And the account user1 should be named "user1"
    And a user logged in space s1 should see 2 PlatformAccount in the database

  Scenario: Adding an account that has an owner grants the owner no access
    When user user1 adds the account of space s2 to space s1
    Then a user logged in space s1 should see 3 PlatformAccount in the database
    And a user logged in space s2 should see 1 Space in the database

content.text:
I've stopped partway through issue 1, because the `anon` revoke crashes the test database. Nothing is committed. The cucumber run didn't produce a usable result.

**What happened.** The first new scenario calls `upsert_accounts_in_space` while not logged in. Postgres aborted (signal 6), then restarted, so every scenario after it failed while the database was recovering.

**What I narrowed it down to,** on the test stack, image `supabase/postgres:17.6.1.106`:

- Any call to a function that `anon` has no EXECUTE on crashes the server. A throwaway function, created and revoked inside a rolled-back transaction, crashed it the same way, so it isn't my code or PostgREST.
- Other errors don't crash it: division by zero, permission denied on a table, and `RAISE … USING ERRCODE = 'insufficient_privilege'` all return normally.
- The server log shows no assertion message.
- After my migration, these three are the only functions in `public` that `anon` can't execute. Nothing in production exercises this today, so I don't know whether hosted Postgres behaves the same. If it does, the revoke would let any unauthenticated client crash the production database. I don't see a safe way to test that against production.

**What I recommend:** drop the revoke from this PR. The editor check already blocks `anon`: `auth.uid()` is NULL, so `in_space` returns false and the function raises `42501`. The revoke would only have been a second layer. The "not logged in" scenario stays, and it should pass through the check. The crash would become its own issue candidate.

**Done so far on `security-upsert-account-requires-editor`:**

- **Schema, `account.sql`:** the editor check, the `SpaceAccess` branch removed, `COMMENT ON` for the three functions, and the three revokes.
- **Migration:** `20261029120000_upsert_account_requires_editor.sql`, restating the same text.
- **Tests:** `features/accountUpsert.feature`, with four scenarios: not logged in, no access, reader access, and an owned account that gains no access. There are four new steps in `stepdefs.ts`.
- **Callers checked:** `upsert_documents`, `upsert_content` and `upsert_concepts` are security invoker, and the Document, Content and Concept insert policies already require `in_space(…, 'editor')`. The new check doesn't block any caller that could have succeeded before.
- **Test database:** the migration is applied with the revokes in place. If we drop them, I'll re-grant EXECUTE to `PUBLIC` and `anon` there, then rerun the suite.

Separately, node v22.23.2 is gone and the suite needs v22.23.4. I've updated my memory note.

Should I drop the revoke, re-grant on the test database and rerun? And do you want an issue candidate for the crash on the Roam page?

No, let's try to understand what's going on. I have updated supabase on a branch, and the old version in main may mismatch the updated database in docker. I went back to the branch, did pnpm install, went back to main; we're now running the more recent version. Can you try the crash again?

The probe refutes the hypothesis: the crash comes from the old image itself, not from a version mismatch.

- **The volume is fresh.** `supabase_db_test` was created at 18:24:42 UTC, and the log shows this image running `initdb` on it then. So it's image `17.6.1.106` running on its own data directory.
- **It still crashes.** The throwaway function crashed the server again (signal 6, then recovery), exactly as before. On `17.11.0.006` the same probe returned `permission denied for function zz_probe`.

This brings the production question back. If the hosted project runs a Postgres build with this bug, the revoke would let an unauthenticated client crash it: one RPC call to any of the three functions. Our migration would introduce the first public functions `anon` can't execute, so nothing in production has hit this path yet.

What would settle it:

1. **Production Postgres version:** you can see it in the Supabase dashboard (Project Settings → Infrastructure), or I can read `select version()` if you give me a read-only way in. At or above the fixed version, the revoke is safe.
2. **Below the fixed version:** either upgrade production first, which is what `eng-2431` heads towards, or ship this fix without the revoke. The editor check already refuses `anon` with `42501`, and the revoke could follow once the upgrade lands.

I also see you've committed the work as `0be07a975` on `security-upsert-account-requires-editor`. The test database is still recovering from the probe and should be back in a few seconds.

Do you want to check the production version, or go straight to splitting the revoke out?
Production: Postgres version is 17.6.1.063 . Not reassuring. So this should stack on eng-2431.

Stacking on `eng-2431` fixes the local stack, but not production. The repo doesn't control the hosted Postgres version. `eng-2431` moves the CLI to 2.122.0, which pulls the `17.11.0.006` image locally, while production stays on `17.6.1.063` until someone upgrades the project in the Supabase dashboard (Infrastructure → upgrade). If the revoke migration deploys before that upgrade, production would have three RPCs that any unauthenticated client can use to crash the database.

We also haven't seen `17.6.1.063` itself crash. It's older than `.106`, so it's probably affected, but that's an assumption. I can test it directly: pull `public.ecr.aws/supabase/postgres:17.6.1.063` and run the same probe in a standalone container. That needs no Supabase stack and doesn't touch `supabase_db_test`.

Whatever that shows, I'd change the shipping order:

1. **This PR, stacked on `eng-2431`:** the editor check, the branch removal and the scenarios, without the revoke. The check already refuses `anon` with `42501`, so the hole is closed.
2. **Production upgrade:** upgrade the hosted Postgres to a version without the crash, as a step in `eng-2431` or its own task.
3. **Revoke follow-up:** a small migration that revokes from `PUBLIC` and `anon`, deployed after the upgrade.

The other path keeps the revoke in this PR and makes the production upgrade a hard precondition for deploying it. That's simpler in the repo, but it relies on deploy order, and nothing in CI would catch it.

input.description:
## Problem

* Production runs Postgres `17.6.1.063`. Upcoming security fixes revoke EXECUTE on public functions from `anon`, starting with the editor-access fix for `upsert_account_in_space` (branch `security-upsert-account-requires-editor`).
* On the local image `17.6.1.106`, calling a public function without EXECUTE on it crashes the Postgres server (signal 6) instead of returning `permission denied`. Postgres then restarts through recovery, and every open connection drops.
* On `17.11.0.006`, the image that ENG-2431 brings to local development, the same call returns `permission denied for function`.
* If production behaves like `17.6.1.106`, one unauthenticated RPC call to a revoked function restarts the production database. No public function is revoked from `anon` today, so production has not hit this path yet.

## Solution

* After ENG-2431 merges, upgrade the production Postgres through the Supabase dashboard (Project Settings → Infrastructure) to at least `17.11.0.006`, the version local development runs.

## Done When

* The dashboard shows production on the new version.
* On a local container of that same image, the probe in Notes returns `permission denied for function` and the server keeps running.
* After the upgrade, Roam and Obsidian sync still work against production.

## Out of Scope

* The revokes themselves. They ship with their own tickets, which this ticket blocks.
* Finding the exact image version that fixed the crash.

## Notes

* Not yet verified: whether `17.6.1.063` itself crashes. A standalone container of that image would settle it.
* The `17.6.1.106` crash reproduced on a freshly initialised volume, so it is not a mismatch between the image and an upgraded data directory.
* Probe, run as `postgres` in one session: `BEGIN; CREATE FUNCTION public.zz_probe() RETURNS int LANGUAGE sql AS 'select 1'; REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.zz_probe() FROM PUBLIC, anon; SET LOCAL ROLE anon; SELECT public.zz_probe(); ROLLBACK;`
* Other errors do not crash `17.6.1.106`: division by zero, permission denied on a table, and `RAISE … USING ERRCODE = 'insufficient_privilege'` all return normally.
* Created with: dg-create-engineering-ticket, dg-engineering-writing-style

content.text:
The fix and the test are written. Nothing has run against the database yet.

**What changed**
- **`account.sql`:** `group_membership_insert_policy` is now just `is_group_admin(group_id)`. I added a `COMMENT ON POLICY` that says how the first admin and invited members get in, since neither goes through this policy.
- **Migration `20261029130000_group_membership_insert_admin_only.sql`:** drops and recreates the policy, and sets the same comment.
- **`features/groupMembership.feature`:** two scenarios.
  1. A reader of s1 tries to escalate to editor. s1 shares itself with my_group, which s2 is in, so the user of s2 can read the s1 user's id from `PlatformAccount` through its own client. It then inserts a membership with that id as `group_id`. The test expects 42501, and expects a document upsert to s1 to fail afterwards.
  2. Taking over an orphaned group: s1's user creates my_group and leaves it, then s2's user tries to join and should fail.
- **`stepdefs.ts`:** three new steps at the end of the file: "leaves group", "fails to add itself to group", and "fails to join the user of space … as a group".
- **Checks:** prettier and tsc pass. eslint and lintSchemas report nothing on the changed lines; the warnings they do print were already there.

**Plan for running cucumber**
1. Move the two stray issue-1 files into the scratchpad. They're committed on `security-upsert-account-requires-editor`, so nothing is lost.
2. Check that `docker ps` shows `supabase_db_test`, then apply the new policy to the running database.
3. Run the full suite.
4. Put the old policy back, run only `groupMembership.feature`, and confirm both scenarios fail. Then reapply the fix.

Shall I go ahead?

One more thing: `group_exists` is now unused. It's a security-definer function that anyone can call, and it tells the caller whether a given id is a group. I'd drop it in this branch, but that also means editing `dbTypes.ts`, so I've left it alone until you decide.
Ah, added the migration to the appropriate commit, and committed the new work. We should be able to run the tests. We could drop group_exists.

input.title: Stop users from joining another user's space access through a group membership
input.description:
## Problem

- Any signed-in user can insert a `group_membership` row whose `group_id` is another user's ID. The access checks (`my_user_accounts()`, and so `in_space`) then give them that user's space access, up to editor.
- Cause: `group_membership_insert_policy` is `is_group_admin(group_id) OR NOT group_exists(group_id)`. The second clause was meant for creating a group, but it passes for any user ID that is not yet a group.
- A user with reader access to a space can read its editor's ID from `SpaceAccess`, so a reader can become an editor. The same clause also lets anyone take over a group after its last member leaves.
- Reproduced locally: under the current rule, a reader of space s1 joined s1's editor as a group and `in_space(s1, 'editor')` went from false to true.

## Solution

- Make the insert rule `is_group_admin(group_id)` only, and drop the then-unused `group_exists` function.
- Nothing needs the removed clause: `create-group` adds the first admin with the service role, and `accept_group_invitation` runs as a security definer.

## Done When

- A Cucumber scenario shows a reader of a space failing to join its editor's ID as a group, and failing to upsert documents to that space afterwards.
- A Cucumber scenario shows that nobody can join a group after its last member leaves.
- Both scenarios fail against the current rule and pass with the fix; the existing group scenarios (create, invite, admin adds member) still pass.

## Out of Scope

- Hiding `SpaceAccess.account_uid` from readers. It stops being exploitable once the insert rule is fixed.

## Notes

- Issue candidate: https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/Wwm8OO2uF
- Implemented on local branch `security-group-membership-insert`, based on `eng-2431-update-supabase-globally`. It adds no `REVOKE`, so it does not wait on ENG-2437.
- Created with: dg-create-engineering-ticket, dg-engineering-writing-style

input.title: Require editor access to a space before adding accounts to it
input.description:
## Problem

- `upsert_account_in_space` is `SECURITY DEFINER` and checks no access. Any caller, including one not logged in, can rename an unowned `PlatformAccount` in any space, link it to the space through `LocalAccess`, and add email identifiers to it. `upsert_accounts_in_space` and `create_account_in_space` call it and share the problem.
- For an account with an owner, the function also adds a `SpaceAccess` row for that owner. Two bugs make that branch fail today. If they were fixed, a caller could give an account they own editor access to any space: `least(my_permissions_in_space(space_id_), 'editor')` returns `editor` when the caller has no access, because `LEAST` ignores NULL.
- That branch should not exist. `LocalAccess` says an account belongs to a space and grants nothing. People will get `SpaceAccess` through their Discourse Graphs account, after its planned verification, not by being listed as an author.

## Solution

- At the start of `upsert_account_in_space`, raise `insufficient_privilege` unless `in_space(space_id_, 'editor')`.
- Remove the `SpaceAccess` branch. The `space_editor` and `permissions` input fields, and `permissions_` of `create_account_in_space`, are then ignored; keep them so existing clients keep working.
- Revoke EXECUTE on the three functions from `PUBLIC` and `anon`. Plugins call them only after logging in.

## Done When

- Cucumber scenarios show that a client that is not logged in, a user with no access to the space, and a user with reader access all fail to add or rename accounts through it, and the account's name is unchanged.
- A Cucumber scenario shows an editor adding an account that has an owner, and the owner gains no access to the space.
- The existing callers still work: document, content and concept upserts (security invoker, editor-only insert rules) and Roam's `upsertUsers`. The full Cucumber suite passes.

## Out of Scope

- An editor of their own space can still rename any account on the same platform through the upsert's name update. This needs its own issue candidate.

# PR adherence check

1. Use the supplied PR or resolve the current branch's PR. Read its title, base and head commits, complete diff, body, checks, and review state. Resolve these from the target repository, not the skill's installation directory. If reviewing changes to the rules themselves, also inspect the base versions so removing a requirement cannot silently erase a finding.
3. Resolve the Linear ticket from an explicit identifier, then the PR or branch. Use the repository's `$scope-check` skill for the `Done When` boundary and its separate Scope check output. Missing ticket access or acceptance criteria blocks the scope conclusion, not independent standards checks.
4. Use command results and manual testing evidence tied to the reviewed revision. A checked box or successful unrelated CI job is not proof of all validation. Record the reviewed head and any local changes so stale evidence is identifiable.

## Evaluate adherence

- Inspect the complete diff and enough surrounding code to assess applicable TypeScript, UI, organization, comments, documentation, hygiene, and testing rules. Focus findings on introduced or modified code, not unrelated existing debt.
- Check title and branch conventions, ticket linkage, PR body requirements, size guidance, split justification, review entry points, testing evidence, Loom, and review/check status against `PR_GUIDELINES.md`.
- Distinguish mandatory rules from preferences. Words such as “prefer” and “ideally,” the 200-line target, and the five-file guideline need judgment. Above 400 changed lines, excluding tests, check for the required explanation and review guide rather than rejecting the size alone.
